What the scores actually say

Three patterns, all consistent across the eighteen renders the tool could take — all of them now scored.

  • Attention climbs through every clip and peaks on the last second. Not one render peaks early. That is the film working as designed — slow builds that pay off — and it is also why the hook column is weak: the Predictor's hook window is seconds 0–3, and this film does not front-load. Do not chase the hook number in the film. Use it for the public post only.
  • The two chroma takes of S22 are the two strongest things in the account — 59 and 58 overall, hooks 43 and 41, viral 60, the lowest mind-wandering of anything (DMN 0.45, 0.46), and the highest visual-cortex drive (0.60). The three “filthy” takes of the same shot score 49, 49 and 55 — and the 55 gets there on audio (auditory 0.53) with the visual channel at 0.39. Same shot, same boys, one grade decision, roughly eight points. Finish the film on 4896c8e3.
  • S18's three-angle temple shot is the one clip that opens strong and decays — both takes peak at second 0 and slide (sustain 92–94 against 100 everywhere else). The internal cuts front-load it. Fine for the film; do not use it for the post.
  • The Oriane "upgraded form" blends are the weakest hooks in the account (28, 28). They are texture, not a shot. Keep S12 on the pull-off-the-hide take.
